steps.content: Walking through familiar streets at a well-known hour, she goes against the flow of the crowd. A quick left and 50 meters more, and there's the Fifth Avenue. There stands the nerve center of Eastside—the towering Eastside TV Station.
A pale figure blends with the crowd, face blank, watching those who, glued to their phones, push their way upstream against the crowd.
The world spins in a listless haze, the clamor of the crowd mingling with unsettling noises.
Gradually, these sounds grow clearer, ringing distinctly in my ears.
Ting-a-ling...
Oh, there you are...
Are you here... to destroy me?

steps.speaker: Eleven
steps.content: Indeed, I am.
But haven't you already ruined enough lives? Isn't that enough? All I have left is... just this little bit of strength...

steps.speaker: Eleven
steps.content: Even a little is unacceptable. This is the root cause... It'll just lead to more of those unwanted problems.
Eleven strides against the crowd, moving swiftly. The jostling shoulders of pedestrians make her wince in pain, but she doesn't stop.

steps.speaker: Eleven
steps.content: It's time to stop; the last call at three in the morning has already ended.

steps.speaker: Eleven
steps.content: I'll make sure no one remembers that there ever was a show or a phone call like this.
Oh? Then what, exactly, is this we're doing right now...?
Eleven makes her way to the base of the TV building, uncovering a hidden black terminal in a nook.
As long as we both exist, there will always be another call coming in at three in the morning...
Another "host" will emerge...
The world will continue to be flooded with sounds you'd rather not hear!
Change is beyond your reach. Forever.
Clack.
The line goes dead on the terminal, echoing with a busy signal. The black device in her grasp turns into a shadowy mist, ascending into the heavens.

steps.speaker: Eleven
steps.content: ...This isn't the real deal.
Eleven gazes upward, the city's neon blaze hiding every star from view.
Yet, she remembered a sky brimming with stars here—that time on the highest rooftop, falling fiercely as if racing the stars.
She extended her hand, but it met only the empty air.

steps.speaker: Eleven
steps.content: Wait, this isn't right...?!

steps.speaker: Eleven
steps.content: That's not me!! I recall... that moment... he had held my hand!
steps.female_content: That's not me!! I recall... that moment... she had held my hand!

steps.content: An instant of reflection, and the atmosphere around begins to warp, something's off.
Eleven's breath catches in terror, feeling as though unseen hands are lifting her, propelling her from the ground floor to the rooftop!

steps.speaker: Eleven
steps.content: Could it be... is it... Mania??

steps.speaker: Eleven
steps.content: Could the real thing... actually be hidden here?

steps.speaker: Malicious Voice
steps.content: Didn't I say you should be laying on the compliments thicker? The more you suck up, the bigger your payoff. Got it?

steps.speaker: Disdainful Voice
steps.content: Controversy fuels fame; it's your chance to shine. Seriously, you're a fan of this, right? This is how you show your affection?

steps.speaker: Eleven
steps.content: ...And it's happening again, making me see all this stuff.
Images that flit across the sight are a mix of the known and the unknown.
They rake up the past Eleven was trying to put behind.
Beep beep beep—
A red alert pops up on your screen. You click to see a red dot blinking on the Dis map.
"Major spike in M-value in Eastside's south! Dispatch now to stop the surge!"
This again?
You check the time on your computer. Seeing it's the dead of night makes your eyelid flicker.
Feels like the Mania in Eastside's gotten worse lately...
But are we all okay, mentally?
Never mind, just the usual grind—more overtime, endless work, and the relentless call of duty.
You snap the file shut, organize it, and head out in your car to the designated spot.
Exiting the Bureau, the guard at the entrance salutes and hands you half of his wife's packed lunch—just a basic sandwich with a runny egg.
The further you drive, the more familiar the surroundings become.
You only twig it when that massive building looms up at your destination.
Trouble at the TV tower again? Don't tell me it's...
The moment you step out of the car, your phone goes off—and it's not just yours. All around, everyone's phones are ringing simultaneously.

steps.speaker: Passerby A
steps.content: Hello? Hello? Anyone there?

steps.speaker: Passerby B
steps.content: What's going on here?

steps.speaker: Passerby C
steps.content: Hello? Bad reception?
Your eyes fix on the terminal, an unknown caller ID lighting up. You swipe the green answer button.
With only the buzz of static filling your ears, you stay wordless, juggling the call while using your real ID to get through the television station's doors.
As you enter the elevator, the phone call's chatter slowly diminishes, giving way to a clear, feminine voice.

steps.speaker: Female Voice Over the Line
steps.content: Head to the roof.
You hit the top floor button, settling into a quiet wait.
Eleven, is that you?
Stirring up a storm here, who else could it be but you?
Looks like we're about to cash in on that goodbye you tossed my way.
How about we discuss a matter, what do you say?
It seems every time we meet, it's during my overtime hours...
How about you hop over to my bureau? Then, our meet-ups wouldn't exactly be overtime, right?
Or maybe you're actually keen on getting back to the TV station, to keep hosting that Call at 3 AM show?

steps.speaker: Female Voice Over the Line
steps.content: Yeah... I've been thinking...

steps.speaker: Female Voice Over the Line
steps.content: You see... I long to hear those voices, yearning for everyone to hear mine...
There's a brief pause on the line, her voice returning, distant and ethereal.

steps.speaker: Female Voice Over the Line
steps.content: To fill this world once more with...
The elevator doors part, casting a weak glow from the energy-saving lights dangling before them, leaving the hallway cloaked in shadows.
There's an unmistakable sense of dread as you stand there. Behind that door to the rooftop, a fearsome Mania energy is lurking, suffocating the air with its ominous presence.
Got it, loud and clear.
You quickly hang up and, with a swift motion, fling the door wide open—
On the empty rooftop, a swirling mass of dark energy wraps tightly around Eleven. She's motionless, eyes closed, seemingly unconscious.
In her grip, there's a terminal, clearly not hers, a bit on the older side. The signal light is still glowing, hinting at an active call.
That was you on the phone just now, right?
But, weirdly enough... it feels like I'm the only one who can hear that voice.
That old trick? I've seen it before in worlds warped by Mania.
Seriously, you don't expect me to fall for that line again, right?
Your eyes are locked on that vintage terminal, with your hands clasped behind you, glowing red, creeping ever closer to Eleven.

steps.speaker: Female Voice Over the Line
steps.content: It's not the same... We're different, in every way...

steps.speaker: Female Voice Over the Line
steps.content: I long for the world to... just once more... just once more...
Eleven!
The lights on that vintage terminal flicker, betraying its unrest. You catch this lapse, casting forth scarlet shackles that wrap tightly around the hands of the one deep in sleep.
Suddenly, a tidal wave of grief overwhelms you, sending a shiver through your body, like falling into a frozen abyss.

steps.speaker: Eleven
steps.content: You're not getting away from me.
Across the shackles, Eleven's eyes flutter open. Your strength stirs her to consciousness, igniting her spirit of defiance.

steps.speaker: Eleven
steps.content: Just vanish... vanish forever, I command you!
Eleven activates her powers, causing the vintage terminal in her hand to break free and rise, as if battling against an unseen force, into mid-air.
The dark mist that has been circling her now rushes towards it, wrapping it in a swirling embrace.
One by one, cracks spread across the terminal's body, punctuated by sharp snaps of breaking. The stubborn red light, which has been flickering all this while, at last fades to darkness.
Eleven, along with the old terminal, collapses to the ground. She lies there, breathing heavily, staring at the terminal with an expression that is a mix of confusion and unreadability.
Thankfully, it didn't lead to anything major this time.
You walk over, slip the terminal into an evidence bag, and then pivot to face Eleven.
So, Miss Eleven, how about...

steps.speaker: Eleven
steps.content: Can you please take me back with you?
Huh?

steps.speaker: Eleven
steps.content: It seems... everything's been taken care of. I had faith in your abilities...

steps.speaker: Eleven
steps.content: There's nothing left for me here now.
Eleven props herself up against the wall, gradually standing up. She brushes off the dust from her clothes and then offers her hand to you.

steps.speaker: Eleven
steps.content: Being a Sinner, it's only expected... that I be held in tight custody.

steps.speaker: Eleven
steps.content: Here... I no longer have a haven.
When you take her hand, the feeling of being linked by those shackles just moments ago is still palpable, undeniable.
Ease up, things here aren't as tough as you're imagining.
At least... you won't be left starving.
Did you get a chance to eat dinner?
Eleven seems unexpectedly taken aback by your question, hesitating briefly before giving a dismissive shake of her head.
Here you go. Go ahead, have a bite.
You hand over the sandwich to Eleven.
My colleague's wife whipped this up. She's got a magic touch, you know—turns even a basic sandwich into something scrumptious.
Guiding Eleven, you step off the elevator.
By the front doors, that video wall you'd glimpsed in the Otherworld remains lit up, as vivid as ever.
On the screen above, a feed cycles through show highlights, timetables, and a handful of bulletins.
Starting today, our regular broadcast "Call at 3 AM" will be on hiatus until further notice. We apologize for any inconvenience and appreciate our audience's patience.
